ENCODING & BYTESFree

HEX to text decoder

Decode hexadecimal bytes to UTF-8 text, or encode text as HEX. Inspect the original bytes even when they are not valid UTF-8.

UTF-8 text & original bytes

Complete byte groups, optionally prefixed with 0x, separated by whitespace.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to translate hexadecimal to text

Each pair of HEX digits represents a byte. A text encoding then determines how those bytes become characters. This tool uses strict UTF-8 for text while retaining valid binary bytes separately.

HEX pairs → bytes → strict UTF-8 text

References: MDN: strict text decoding · MDN: UTF-8 encoding

Good to know

Why is my HEX input rejected?

Each whitespace-separated group must contain an even number of hexadecimal digits, optionally after 0x. Characters outside 0–9 and A–F, empty prefixes, commas and incomplete bytes are rejected rather than guessed.

Why do valid bytes produce no text?

A valid HEX representation can contain binary data or text in another encoding. For example, fb ff ef is valid HEX but invalid UTF-8. The tool keeps the HEX and original bytes available without inventing replacement text.

Is this the same as converting a number?

No. Here 41 is the byte 0x41, which is the character A in UTF-8. Converting the hexadecimal number 41 to decimal would produce the number 65. Those are different tasks.

Do Chinese characters and emoji work?

Yes. Text is encoded as UTF-8 bytes before HEX output. Decoding requires valid UTF-8. An initial U+FEFF character is preserved rather than silently removed.

What are the size limits?

HEX input is limited to 5,000,000 characters and 1,000,000 decoded bytes. Text input is limited to 250,000 UTF-16 code units. Output formatting uses the same original bytes.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Complete byte examples

Choose the interpretation that matches your source data.

HEXUTF-8 result
48 65 6c 6c 6fHello
0x48 0x65 0x6c 0x6c 0x6fThe same bytes with prefixes
e4 b8 ad e6 96 87中文
f0 9f 91 8b👋
fb ff efValid bytes; not UTF-8 text
4 8Rejected: incomplete byte groups

The byte download does not transform or repair data. For example, c3 28 is a valid pair of HEX bytes but invalid UTF-8: the byte following C3 is not a continuation byte. Deleting one byte or replacing the error with a guessed character changes the data. Keep the original byte download and check the source encoding. To inspect URL-safe encoded bytes, use the Base64URL decoder. The encoding troubleshooting guide explains why a valid encoding does not establish a text or image format.
